quote.text: If you are not embarrassed by the first version of your product, you've launched too late.

term.name: Net revenue retention (NRR)
term.def: How much revenue you keep and grow from last year's customers, counting upgrades and losses. Over 100% means existing customers spend more each year, even with zero new sales.

stories.headline: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion
stories.summary: Bending Spoons is buying Mailchimp for $3.31 billion in cash plus $368 million in stock, with the deal expected to close in early 2027. Intuit paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021, and Mailchimp's revenue was $313 million last quarter, down 1% from a year earlier.
stories.takeaway: A beloved brand with flat growth gets valued like one. Brand love is great, but buyers pay for growth, so marketing has to show up in the numbers.

stories.headline: Palo Alto Networks is buying Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
stories.summary: The security giant is paying $4.5 billion in stock for Applied Compute. The young company hit about $100 million in annualized revenue within 18 months of being founded, and could add more than $1 billion of ARR by fiscal 2029.
stories.takeaway: Big platforms buy speed. When a startup grows this fast, the incumbent's pitch shifts from "we built it" to "we bought the best and plugged it in."

stories.headline: TPG and Corpay take BILL private in a roughly $6 billion deal
stories.summary: Private equity firm TPG will pay $63.25 a share in cash for BILL, the small-business payments and spend software company, a 31% premium. Payments company Corpay is putting in $1.1 billion for about a third of the equity, with an option to buy the rest later.
stories.takeaway: When a strategic partner co-invests, expect bundling next. Watch for BILL and Corpay to start selling together to the same finance teams.

stories.headline: Levenza launches enterprise AI agents with 170% net revenue retention
stories.summary: Levenza made its personal AI agents for Teams, Slack and Outlook available worldwide and named customers like Oliver Wyman, Kearney and Spencer Stuart among 300+ users. It says it is profitable without outside funding, with 170% net revenue retention, and users report saving up to three hours a day.
stories.takeaway: Look at how the launch is built: named logos, a retention stat and a time-saved claim. That trio is a classic B2B proof stack.

stories.headline: Microsoft lets AI agents join your company like an employee
stories.summary: With Microsoft Foundry, companies can set agents up as named Microsoft 365 members with their own identity, email, calendar and OneDrive, plus a human manager who is accountable for them. Microsoft also added governance tools for managing whole fleets of agents.
stories.takeaway: "Every agent has a manager" is a trust message aimed at IT and security buyers. Selling AI to enterprises is often about control, not cleverness.

stories.headline: LangChain opens a gateway to keep agent tool use in check
stories.summary: LangChain's LangSmith Tool Gateway is in public beta. It puts credentials, access rules, approvals and audit trails for agent tool calls in one place, and comes with hosted connectors for Google, Microsoft, Salesforce and GitHub.
stories.takeaway: Developer tools win enterprises by adding the boring stuff: permissions, approvals and audit logs. That's what moves a deal from pilot to purchase.

stories.headline: Databricks' new agent fixes broken data pipelines for you
stories.summary: Databricks announced Genie ZeroOps in public beta. The agent figures out why a data pipeline failed and proposes a fix as a pull request, but a human still has to approve changes to production.
stories.takeaway: Notice the "human approves" line. Positioning AI as a helper with a safety catch calms the buyers who would otherwise block it.

stories.headline: OpenAI quietly tests always-on agents in ChatGPT
stories.summary: OpenAI is testing "Dots," agents that keep running in the background, with a small group of ChatGPT Plus users, and rolling it out to eligible Business Standard workspaces.
stories.takeaway: Testing with a small group first is a go-to-market move too. You learn what message lands before the big launch.

stories.headline: UL Solutions is buying sustainability platform Worldly
stories.summary: UL Solutions, known for safety testing and certification, agreed to buy Worldly at an enterprise value of about $350 million. Worldly provides sustainability data software.
stories.takeaway: A testing company buying a data platform is a bet that software can sell alongside services. Pairing the two gives buyers one vendor instead of two.

stories.headline: SAP closes its TechWolf deal to sharpen skills data
stories.summary: SAP completed its purchase of TechWolf for an undisclosed price. TechWolf's "context graph" will help ground the skills data inside SAP SuccessFactors and its Joule AI assistant.
stories.takeaway: AI assistants are only as good as the data behind them. More and more vendors market their data foundation, not just the chatbot on top.
